- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly above recent mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is below recent mean, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +15% above recent peak), reduce forecast by 10–20% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean reverts to historical range within 5–7 days, adjust downward if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently > 10% above true outcome, apply downward bias correction based on sentiment decay (e.g., sentiment < 0.4 → reduce by 5–8%).  
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (alternating +/– values), reduce forecast smoothing weight for short-term spikes.
